items.title: Renting in England as a newcomer
items.summary: What a tenancy is now, what you can be asked to pay, and what to have ready.
body: Since 1 May 2026 a new tenancy in England is an assured periodic tenancy: it rolls on, month to month, with no end date, and you give notice when you want to leave.

On a tenancy, a landlord or agent can only ask for the payments the Tenant Fees Act permits: the rent, a holding deposit of up to a week's rent, and a refundable deposit (five weeks' rent, or six from £50,000 a year).
Have your passport or visa ready for a Right to Rent check, and proof of income or a guarantor if you are new to the UK.

items.title: A first week in Marylebone
items.summary: Where to shop, walk and eat while you settle in.
body: Start with the park: the Outer Circle is a good morning walk, and the rose garden is ten minutes from the door.
The High Street has what you need for the week, and the Sunday market behind it is worth an early visit.

visitInfo.payment: Stays are paid by our own payment link; rent by bank transfer. We never change our bank details by email; call us before paying if anything looks different.

questions.q: Is the price I see the price I pay?
questions.a: Yes. Every total includes the nightly rate with service and VAT and the final clean. Nothing is added at the end.

questions.q: Can I stay longer than three months?
questions.a: Yes, on a rolling tenancy priced by the month. Slide the stay bar to Long let to see the rent and the deposit.

questions.q: Can I arrive late at night?
questions.a: Yes. The concierge is in until midnight and a night porter after that; tell us your flight or train.
Each home's details say which side it faces, its glazing, cooling and blinds.
